import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I wrote a plan for the `\` → `#` alias. It passed validation and `sase plan propose` has staged it for your approval. No code has changed in either repo, and no finalizer declaration was needed.

**How it works:** it extends the same bob rule (`expand_sigil_alias`) that handles `.` → `^` and `;` → `:`. bob swaps `\` for `#` only where its completion grammar says a real `#` would open a menu. I ran today's `bob capture-complete` on a throwaway vault, and these are the spots where `#` opens one:

| You type | Becomes | Menu |
|---|---|---|
| `Buy milk \` | `Buy milk #` | task type |
| `@cash\` | `@cash#` | section |
| `@cash+goog-exit\` | `@cash+goog-exit#` | drawer |
| `@cash^goog-exit@` ⏎ `- \` | `- #` | drawer bullet |
| `@cash:goog-exit\`, `=25\`, `x=25\` | `…#` | Pomodoro name / start / past |
| `=/\`, `=*fix\`, `[[cash\` | `…#` | split type, merge destination, wikilink heading |

I also checked the alias against simulated drafts: `\` stays literal at line starts, glued to a word (`C:\`, `dir\`), mid-line, in Work Log text, and right after another `\`.

**Your two rules:**
- **Line starts:** a `\` with only whitespace before it never becomes `#`. On a blank draft it still opens Go To as `/`. At the start of any later line it stays a plain `\`, so a `#type` at the start of a line still needs a real `#`. A bullet start (`- \`) doesn't count as a line start, which is what lets `- \` open drawers.
- **Second `\`:** Mac Capture remembers the `#` bob just inserted, the same way the Go To double-tap works. The next `\` turns that `#` back into one literal `\` and closes the type or drawer menu. Any other key cancels this. ⌘Z still restores the `\` you typed.

**Things you might want to change before approving:**
- **Escapes get one more keystroke.** Wherever the alias fires, typing a `\#`, `\%` or `\>` escape now means pressing `\` twice first (`\` `\` `#` → `\#`). If you type `#` straight after the alias you get `##`. The plan doesn't try to detect escapes, because the app would need to know which characters bob treats as escapable, and the app isn't supposed to know grammar.
- **A very fast double-tap leaves `\\`.** If the second `\` lands before bob answers the first (a few milliseconds), the draft keeps both backslashes and no menu opens. The plan accepts this rather than queueing keystrokes, and adds a test so the result is always the same.

The plan has no reviewer decisions; send feedback if you meant something different by "beginning of the line".
